aid: None listed

aid: National Merit $2,500 scholarships; corporate- and college-sponsored scholarships (many colleges add large merit awards for Finalists)
notes: Selection Index = (2 x Reading/Writing score + Math score)/10, max 228. No application fee; entry is via the test.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
eligibility: U.S. citizens or permanent residents residing in the U.S. (or stationed overseas on active U.S. military duty), age 18 or younger as of the application deadline; teams of up to 2 allowed (must email program first)
aid: $100,000, $50,000, or $25,000 scholarships (awarded annually; multiple Fellows each year)
notes: Categories: Science (incl. biology), Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, Literature, Music, Philosophy, and Outside the Box. Two-part application via Submittable (initial eligibility portion, then full materials incl. category requirements + nominators). All applicants notified on or before July 15. Submissions screened for plagiarism and AI-generated text. Applicants/parents must commit to attending the DC awards reception.

name: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS)
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12 enrolled in public, private, or home schools in the U.S., Puerto Rico, and DoD schools; must compete in their assigned regional symposium (Connecticut has its own region)
cost: Free (no cost to register for or participate in regional events)
aid: Regional: ~$4,500 in tuition scholarships per region; National: up to $12,000 in undergraduate scholarships per oral category plus poster awards and travel for national finalists
notes: Categories at nationals: Biomedical Sciences, Chemistry, Engineering & Technology, Environmental Science, Life Sciences, Math & Computer Sciences, Medicine & Health/Behavioral Sciences, Physical Sciences. Requires 250-word abstract and research paper; Statement of Outside Assistance form required. Oral presentations are ~12 minutes with judging panel. Regional dates vary - check the Connecticut region page (jshs.org/state/ct) in fall 2026.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
eligibility: Students in grades 9-12 (or equivalent) who have not reached age 20 on or before May 1 preceding ISEF; must qualify by winning at an affiliated fair (research limited to 12 months of continuous work)
cost: Free to enter; finalist registration paid by the affiliated fair (student covers travel if not subsidized)
aid: Nearly $9M in awards: $100,000 George D. Yancopoulos Innovator Award, two $75,000 Regeneron Young Scientist Awards, plus category awards, scholarships, and internships
notes: ISEF 2027: May 8-14, 2027, Los Angeles Convention Center. Finalist questionnaires due 12 days after fair results; abstract rewrite deadline April 16, 2027. More than 365 affiliated fairs worldwide. Gordon E. Moore Award ($50,000) also offered. Strong synergy with the same research project used for STS, JSHS, and Davidson Fellows.

name: National Science Bowl (NSB)

cost: Free (no registration fee; teams cover travel to regionals/nationals)
aid: National champion team wins a trip to DOE's National Renewable Energy Laboratory; top teams receive trophies/medals and all-expenses-paid trips to nationals (recognition-driven, not cash)
notes: Registration is done by the coach (teacher) via the regional coordinator - students cannot register themselves; schools may enter up to 3 teams if the regional allows. Regionals are assigned by geography. Questions cover biology, chemistry, Earth and space science, energy, mathematics, and physics at college-freshman level (AP-level study helps). 35+ year history; 350,000+ students have participated.

aid: None
